pr.title: gh-143200: fix UAFs in `Element.__{set,get}item__` when the element is concurrently mutated

     def test_treebuilder_start(self):
         # Issue #27863

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+:mod:`xml.etree.ElementTree`: fix use-after-free crashes in
+:meth:`~object.__getitem__` and :meth:`~object.__setitem__` methods of
+:class:`~xml.etree.ElementTree.Element` when the element is concurrently
+mutated. Patch by Bénédikt Tran.

review_comments.body: I am not sure that such comments are useful. They distract future readers, and they are trivial after the bug has been discovered and fixed. We don't add multiline comment for every defensive check, only when they are not obvious. An in this case it is obvious -- due to `self->extra->length` in the next line.

```suggestion
```

The check is directly related to the next line.
This is not related to clearing `self->extra`. The extra could be initially empty.

It is not correct to apply `PySlice_AdjustIndices()` twice. It can correct invalid negative index twice.

Ensure that it is called once in each branch.

BTW, if the extra was just created, it is empty, and calling `PySlice_AdjustIndices()` should not have effect.
The suggestion is about removing a blank line right?

Fair enough, though I'm not sure it's directly obvious that `extra` could change before and after the call but I'll remove the comment (after reconsideration, it looks better to have no comment rather than overly verbose ones)

Move this immediately before `PySlice_AdjustIndices()`. No need to check/create the extra twice.

Actually, in case of deletion, no need to create the extra at all. You can just return without change.
